checkpoints.description: Task 'ui-lifecycle-delivery-v1' completed successfully.

[1/2] Add the git-delivery authorization gate to PRINCIPLE-006 and PRINCIPLE-018, record ADR-162 with its cross-principle check, and document host policy parity. [2/2] Update the pinned tests and run every Phase 4 gate.

impact_assessment.why: PRINCIPLE-006 R1 and PRINCIPLE-018 R1 require milestone commits unconditionally, while host platforms such as Kilo forbid commits the user did not explicitly request, so the Tier 1 capsule contradicts the host on every task.
impact_assessment.benefits: One decidable authorization test replaces ad-hoc conflict handling, and the crash-safe milestone workflow survives on hosts that permit it.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: PRINCIPLE-006 and PRINCIPLE-018 rule text and capsules gain a git-delivery authorization condition; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none, the ledger schema is unchanged.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Update both invariants and R1 branches, update every pinned test, record ADR-162, and run the full Phase 4 gate set.

checkpoints.description: [milestone 1/2] Added the git-delivery authorization gate to PRINCIPLE-006 and PRINCIPLE-018, recorded ADR-162, and documented host policy parity; uncommitted because this host forbids unrequested commits.
[milestone 2/2] Updates pinned tests and runs the full Phase 4 gate set; no commit is made because the host forbids unrequested commits (ADR-162).

Review findings fixed: split commit delivery from push delivery in PRINCIPLE-018 R1/R4, required Phase 4 to pass before the unauthorized milestone checkpoint, and updated the ADR and tests. Unit tier 382/382 pass; integration 49/49 functionally pass but its budget is 253.20ms per test vs the 250ms ceiling (also red at HEAD: 278.12ms, so pre-existing on this host). Uncommitted by PRINCIPLE-018 R1.
Task 'git-delivery-authorization-v1' abandoned: Superseded by adr-review-fixes-v1; the ADR-162 changes remain uncommitted in the working tree.

[1/6] Correct the hygiene scanner: exclude os.open from open-context and make Popen's bounded-wait rule satisfiable, with regression tests. [2/6] Replace stale agent-facing limits: tester/runbook 200ms -> 250ms, reviewer 20,000 -> 22,500 chars, sync comment, then re-sync. [3/6] Bring the integration tier back under 250ms by removing unnecessary UI shell spawns without weakening assertions. [4/6] Align delivery readiness and repair: status --exit-code blocks an open UI task, and reconcile_readme_tree matches exact tree entries. [5/6] Close secret-scan blind spots: scan merge-resolution diffs and drop over-broad whole-file skips where the scanner stays clean. [6/6] Harden rename track classification and the unreadable-ledger save path; add the low-risk UI style and artifact suffix coverage.

impact_assessment.why: The ADR review found a red Phase 4 budget, an unsatisfiable Popen rule, over-broad os.open flagging, stale agent-facing limits, a broken README tree repair, a delivery-readiness disagreement, secret-scan blind spots, and state/track edge cases.
impact_assessment.benefits: Phase 4 becomes green on this host, the hygiene and secret gates describe their actual contracts, agent-facing docs stop contradicting the rules, aikit fix repairs the README tree in one pass, and the ledger/push paths fail safely.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: status --exit-code gains an open-UI-task failure, the hygiene scanner changes which calls it flags, and scan_commits may add merge findings; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: save_ledger now propagates an unreadable on-disk ledger instead of overwriting it.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add failing-first unit and integration tests for each change, record ADR-163 with the scanner and status contract changes, update help and knowledge/services.md, and run every Phase 4 gate.

checkpoints.description: [milestone 1/6] Implemented the scanner Popen/os.open correction, 250ms/22,500-character agent docs, UI test budget work, status/tree readiness fixes, secret-scan widening, rename/ledger hardening, and style/artifact coverage; uncommitted under PRINCIPLE-018 R1.

[milestone 6/6] Phase 4 passed: 388 unit tests at 5.99ms/test and 49 integration tests at 240.67ms/test; sync, knowledge, secrets, reachability and dogfood green; ADR-163 recorded. checklists: passed. Uncommitted because the host forbids unrequested commits.

[milestone 6/6] Verification re-run: 388 unit tests passed; 49 integration tests passed functionally at 252.55ms/test, over the 250ms ceiling; sync, knowledge, secrets, reachability and dogfood passed. checklists: failed PRINCIPLE-010 R6 (integration budget). Uncommitted because the host forbids unrequested commits.

[milestone 6/6] Verification under current host load: 388 unit and 49 integration tests pass functionally, but budgets are unit 9.91ms>8.00, integration 301.73ms>250.00, and dogfood --help 212ms>200; sync, knowledge, secrets and reachability pass. The same tree measured 5.99ms, 240.67ms and 123-131ms earlier, so the failure tracks host load, not the diff. checklists: failed PRINCIPLE-010 R5/R6. Uncommitted.

[1/5] Add a bounded-wait check for Popen so an unbounded wait is flagged, with regression tests. [2/5] Restrict commit delivery authorization to a commit or pull request, leaving a push-only request to authorize only the push; update GUIDELINES, ADR-162 and pins. [3/5] Trim the UI integration test to the real-git style/snapshot proof, move the remaining assertions to the unit tier, and record the begin assertion there. [4/5] Deduplicate merge-scan findings, explain an open UI task in status output, and give an unreadable-ledger save a Why/Fix CLI error. [5/5] Correct ADR-163's overclaims and re-run Phase 4.

impact_assessment.why: Verification of the first fix set exposed an unbounded-Popen blind spot, a push-implies-commit ambiguity, an unstable integration budget, a duplicate merge finding, a silent status failure and a raw ledger I/O error.
impact_assessment.benefits: The hygiene gate catches unbounded Popen again, a push request cannot silently authorize a commit on a restrictive host, the integration tier regains headroom, and delivery failures explain themselves.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: PRINCIPLE-018 R1 no longer treats a push-only request as commit authorization; the hygiene scanner gains a popen-wait-timeout rule and the integration test relies on unit coverage for allow/finish; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: ledger I/O errors are wrapped for the CLI.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add failing-first tests for each behavior, keep the real-git style/lost-control proof, update ADR-162/ADR-163, and run the full Phase 4 set.
